items.title: David Brinkley Interview, 1962-01-10
items.q: Tonight, it features George Lewis on the clarinet. He is just back from a concert tour in Europe.

ctx.x: Jazz here in Bourbon Street is what people seem to think is going to sell drinks. What we're trying to do here is just present the music the way the men want to play it. The people are sitting on wooden benches, sitting on the floor. There's no drinks. It's pretty hot in there too in the summer. People come to hear just the music. I think the men realize this. The men play it the way they want to play it. People hear it. We have a rather selective audience. People come in. All we ask for is something in the…
Tonight, it features George Lewis on the clarinet. He is just back from a concert tour in Europe.

People in New Orleans accept this music on a different social basis than people do all over the world. All over, it's accepted as a form of American culture. In New Orleans, it's a form of music that grew out of a red light district. It's music that people still associate with the problems here.
